label: rem:hecke-charge-mass-duality
title: Charge--mass duality via the Frobenius pairing
html:
The mass integrand \alpha_\varrho = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho splits along two orthogonal directions in the Hecke algebra, corresponding to the two Markov moves of the braid group.

Restriction Markov move H_n(R, q) element Physical invariant
Horizontal Conjugation (within a fibre) \rho(\beta) Charge Q, crossing energy \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}
Vertical Stabilisation (along the tower) \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) Mass \mathfrak{m} = \lvert \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)) \rvert
Mixed Both simultaneously Y(a, z) (vertex operator) Full particle data

The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle_F = \int_A \mu(a \otimes b) mediates the duality: it pairs \mu (horizontal) with \int_A (vertical).

Horizontal restriction (conjugation, within a fibre). Restricting to a single level of the brane tower — crossings within V^{\otimes n} with no tower propagation — the Hecke element \rho(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) encodes the crossing structure directly. The crossing energy (crossing energy) reads off the Skein eigenvalue sum \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} = n_+ q - n_- q^{-1}, and the Coulomb charge (Coulomb charge) is the crossing asymmetry Q = \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-). These are horizontal invariants: they depend on the braiding pattern, not on the depth of the tower.

Vertical restriction (stabilisation, along the tower). The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) (Hecke mass element) dresses \rho(\beta) with the Frobenius--comultiplication operator (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta, which projects through the Frobenius form (collapsing tower data) and comultiplies (probing the tower depth). Its Markov trace (mass via Markov trace) gives the categorical mass \mathfrak{m} = \lvert \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)) \rvert, a vertical invariant measuring resistance to transport through the comultiplication.

Mixed: the vertex operator as generating function. On the mixture — when horizontal crossings and vertical tower steps act simultaneously — the result is the vertex operator Y(a, z) (vertex operator), whose modes

  a_m
  =
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\check{R}_{(a)}\, z^m\bigr)

combine horizontal braiding (\check{R}, the R-matrix) with vertical insertion (z^m, the tower coordinate on \mathcal{S}_p). The vertex operator is the generating function that encodes both charge and mass data simultaneously.

The Frobenius pairing as mediator. The duality between horizontal and vertical is mediated by the Frobenius pairing (Frobenius pairing):

  \langle a, b \rangle_F
  =
  \textstyle\int_A \mu(a \otimes b),

which pairs multiplication \mu (horizontal: composing crossings) with the Frobenius form \int_A (vertical: integrating along the tower). This pairing identifies the particle element \rho(\beta) (charge carrier) with the mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) (mass carrier) as dual aspects of a single Hecke algebra element, connected by exactly the Frobenius--comultiplication map that defines the categorical mass.
